hook.text: Mendel got lucky. Pea traits happen to follow simple rules. If he'd studied height in humans, he might have quit.

buildup.text: His seven pea traits are each controlled by single genes on different chromosomes. Perfect for discovering clean laws.

discovery.text: Most traits in nature are messier—multiple genes, environmental effects, partial dominance. Mendel found the exception.

twist.text: Some historians suspect Mendel's data was too perfect. The ratios fit predictions almost impossibly well.

climax.text: Whether luck or bias, his conclusions held. Modern genetics confirmed every law he proposed. The monk was right.

punchline.text: He picked the right organism and asked the right questions.

quiz.question: Why were pea plants ideal for Mendel's experiments?
options: Key traits are controlled by single genes
